doc: What a model has that a registered class does NOT compute. A class is one function: token ids in, next-token logits (or a pooled embedding) out. A model that also takes images or audio, or predicts several tokens at once, has parts this class leaves out; the scope says so, in the pack, in preflight and in `misaka model inspect`, and never presents a partial reading as the whole. A rule matches by configuration keys, tensor-name prefixes or substrings, or the names of files beside the checkpoint (a GGUF's mmproj). Any one match is evidence.

rules.why: image input is not part of a class: the registered class is the text decoder, token ids in and logits out, so a prompt cannot carry an image
the projector maps vision or audio features into the decoder's embedding space; with no tower to feed it, it is not computed
audio input is not part of a class: the registered class is the text decoder
extra heads that propose further tokens (speculative decoding); the next-token distribution is the main head's, so the class does not need them
a draft model is a second network that proposes tokens for the main one; the class is the main network alone
